description: Ring membership for agent canary rollout (initiative #495, issues #500/#501). The promotion automation (scripts/canary-rollout.sh) reads this as the single source of truth. `next` is host-relative: it resolves to the repo that HOSTS the reusable; `ring0` covers the other org-infra repo (the host already sits in `next`).

member_tokens.$host: the agent's host repo (the repo that owns the reusable)
member_tokens.$org_infra: org_infra_repos minus the host (the host is already in `next`)
member_tokens.*: every other consumer not named in an earlier ring

_agent_ref_paths_note: agent_ref_paths (#1019): the host-relative paths a consumer EXECUTES at its pinned channel tag BEYOND the reusable workflow blob — the reusable checks these out at `agent_ref` (e.g. scripts/, prompts/, personas/). autocut's change detection and the `drift` ship-drift report watch the reusable PLUS these paths, so a script-only change is no longer invisible (a merged-but-not-shipped change reaches nobody). This top-level list is the fleet default; an agent may override with `.agents[<a>].agent_ref_paths`. Patterns ending in `/` match by directory prefix.
_autocut_note: autocut (#1069): `canary-rollout.sh autocut` (gated by org var CANARY_AUTO_CUT) auto-cuts a new immutable <agent>/vX.Y.Z + moves `next` when a reusable's blob on its host main HEAD differs from the current `next` candidate. Since #712 (epic #1083 pillar 2) the bump is DETECTED from the change: a conventional-commit `!`/`BREAKING CHANGE` or a `workflow_call` interface break (removed/renamed input|secret, or a newly-required input) → major (seeding a fresh v<newMAJOR>-next per #657 F4); a non-breaking `feat` → minor; else patch. The optional `.agents[<a>].autocut.bump` knob (patch|minor|major) is now an OVERRIDE that forces a level (not the sole source); it fails safe to patch on any signal-fetch error.

gate._standard: petry-projects/.github#548 — graduated dwell/sample gate over a per-candidate cumulative window. These are registry-configurable per-transition knobs; the values below are the #548 defaults.

benign_failure_classes.reason: #864/#668 — a Dev-Lead run dispatched in a Dependabot context receives no Actions secrets and fails at startup, before any candidate code executes; inherently version-independent (can never be candidate-caused), so excluded even when the candidate changed the reusable (differs=1).
fix-review git push denied by branch protection / missing write scope; version-independent benign failure, not a candidate regression.

gate._benign_note: benign_failure_classes (#1025 P2): per-reusable allowlist matched against a failed run's workflow name (`workflow` ERE) + failed-step signature (`step` ERE, matched via `gh run view`). Matches are excluded from cum_fail — but ONLY when the candidate's reusable is byte-identical to the prior channel (differs=0), so the allowlist can never mask a candidate-introduced regression. Exception (#668): a class marked `version_independent: true` fails before/independent of the candidate's own code (e.g. a Dependabot-context secrets failure at startup) and can NEVER be candidate-caused, so it is excluded even when differs=1 — reserve the flag for classes where that is provable from the failure mechanism, not merely likely. `control.allow_pre_existing`, or `promote --allow-pre-existing`, advances a BLOCKED+PRE_EXISTING frontier (never REGRESSION).

suspect_failure_classes.reason: #664/#668 — a dev-lead run can exit 124 when a stage exceeds its time budget (large workload, or a rebase-conflict sentinel that never resolves). This is *possibly* candidate-caused (a candidate that changed execution-time-sensitive code could genuinely be slower), so unlike a version_independent benign class it is NOT auto-cleared — it BLOCKS as SUSPECT and carries a discriminating question for a fast human confirm.
suspect_failure_classes.guidance: Did this candidate change execution-time-sensitive code, or is it a large-workload/rebase timeout unrelated to the diff? If unrelated → `promote --override`; if the candidate got materially slower → treat as a real regression and roll back.

gate._suspect_note: suspect_failure_classes (#668 increment 2): same shape as benign classes (`id`, `workflow` ERE, `step` ERE) plus a `guidance` discriminating question. A counted (non-benign) failure that matches a suspect class at differs=1 is triaged SUSPECT instead of REGRESSION — it still BLOCKS and still needs a human (labelled `needs-human`, NOT auto-cleared like `version_independent`), but the blocker issue renders the `guidance` so the human confirm is a 30-second check rather than a from-scratch investigation. Default-absent (this key omitted) = today's behavior, byte-identical for agents that do not opt in.
gate._confirm_note: require_confirmation (#668 increment 3, Layer 3): opt-in human go/no-go at ONE ring boundary for a correctness-sensitive agent. When a transition sets `require_confirmation: true` and the reliability verdict is otherwise PROMOTE, the frontier holds in state AWAITING_CONFIRMATION — the scheduled promote-all never auto-advances it; a deliberate `promote <agent> --confirm` dispatch (Actions-audit-logged) does. The confirmation IS the dispatch (no state store). `--confirm` is NOT `--override`: it advances ONLY a reliability-clean AWAITING_CONFIRMATION state and can never bypass a BLOCKED gate. sync-issues files an evidence-carrying `canary-confirm:<agent>` issue (compare diff link + run stats; labelled `needs-human`) that auto-closes on promote or candidate change. dev-lead only initially; reliability still clears next/ring0/ring1 unattended. Default-absent (this key omitted) = fully autonomous, byte-identical for agents that do not opt in.

benign_failure_classes.reason: #943 — the run failed at 'Set up job' with 'Failed to resolve action download info: Error: Service Unavailable' while the runner was fetching action metadata from GitHub's backend, retried twice with backoff, then gave up — entirely before checkout or any candidate reusable step ran. Confirmed environmental: the SAME candidate/failure evaluated for the next->ring0 transition (differs=0 there) was independently auto-triaged PRE_EXISTING, and 14+ surrounding runs on the same candidate all succeeded. NOT version_independent: the matcher (_run_signature) only sees failed step NAMES, never log content, so a bare 'Set up job' signature could equally arise from a candidate breaking the reusable's own YAML (e.g. a bad `uses:` ref failing action resolution) — matching add-to-project's reusable-setup-restricted-secrets class. This class therefore excludes only at differs=0 (byte-identical candidate) and can never mask a differs=1 regression; a differs=1 occurrence of this exact outage (like #943's ring1->stable) still needs a human `promote --override` with the run evidence.

gate._correctness_note: correctness (#668 increment 4, Layer 2): opt-in DECISION telemetry on organic runs — the actual correctness signal. pr-auto-review emits one no-op `decision: <class>` step per outcome branch (dispatched / skip-draft / skip-checks-pending / skip-changes-requested / skip-unresolved-threads); only the taken branch runs, the rest skip. The engine tallies the candidate's decision mix on the source tier (per-candidate window) against a prior-version baseline (source tier, pre-cut trailing window) — both read from `gh run view --json jobs` step names, prefix-matched by `decision_step_prefix`. `decide_decision_shift` returns OK|SHIFT|INSUFFICIENT: INSUFFICIENT (either sample below its min, or absent/unparseable decision steps) is a NO-OP that degrades to reliability-only, so low-traffic agents never stall on a signal they can't produce; SHIFT (any decision class's share moves ≥ max_shift_permille per-mille) HOLDS the promotion with triage SUSPECT (correctness variant) and sync-issues renders a candidate-vs-baseline decision-mix table in the blocker issue; OK is a no-op. Never rolls back, never auto-acts — SHIFT only holds (worst case: a few hours of human latency). Gross always/never/gross shifts only, by design (n=10–25). Default-absent (this key omitted) = today's behaviour, byte-identical for agents that do not opt in.

pr-review._note: petry-projects/.github#1166 — the ring-0 self-host reviewer (#497). Its engine reusable `pr-review.yml` (grandfathered legacy name, #1127) lives in .github-private and is dogfooded there on `pr-review/next` via the `pr-review-trigger.yml` caller stub. It was absent from the registry, so autocut never cut/advanced its channel and a merged fix sat inert on main until a human ran cut-release.sh (two incidents in three days). run_workflow is the caller stub's DISPLAY NAME (the `name:` of pr-review-trigger.yml), NOT the engine or a *.yml filename: a workflow_call-only reusable has no runs of its own, so the gate reads the caller's run history via `gh run list --workflow`. It must be the display name because a repo without this workflow (every tier beyond the .github-private self-host) then returns the graceful 'could not find any workflows named …' (→ [], #747), whereas a *.yml filename would 404 and be mis-triaged as a transient fetch failure that fails the gate CLOSED. Registered host-relative like dev-lead/ci-failure-analyst: `next` = the host, so `next`+`ring0` span both org-infra repos. The self-host circular dependency (#497) is bounded by the soak gate — a candidate that breaks reviews on `next` (.github-private) fails there and is BLOCKED, never reaching ring0/stable.
